[edit]

  • Rhymes: -io
  • Syllabification(key): do‧mi‧ni‧o

Noun

[edit]

dominio

  1. (historical) Dominion

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin dominium.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /doˈmi.njo/
  • Rhymes: -injo
  • Hyphenation: do‧mì‧nio

Noun

[edit]

dominio m (plural domini)

  1. rule, dominion
  2. power
  3. control
  4. mastery
  5. (biology, taxonomy) domain
    • 2015, Adelphi Edizioni, transl., Origini: La storia scientifica della creazione, Adelphi Edizioni spa, translation of original by Jim Baggott, published 2017, →ISBN:
      Oltre al dominio dei batteri, vi è anche un dominio di «archibatterri», o semplicemente «archei».
      Besides the domain of bacteria, there is also a domain of "archaebacteria", or simply "archaea"

Further reading

[edit]

  • dominio in garzantilinguistica.it – Garzanti Linguistica, De Agostini Scuola Spa

Anagrams

[edit]
  • monoidi, odonimi, ominido

Latin

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

dominiō

  1. dative/ablative singular of dominium

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Learned borrowing from Latin dominium. Cognate with English dominion and domain.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /doˈminjo/ [d̪oˈmi.njo]
  • Rhymes: -injo
  • Syllabification: do‧mi‧nio

Noun

[edit]

dominio m (plural dominios)

  1. domain
  2. rule, dominion
  3. dominance, domination, power, control
  4. mastery
    Synonym: maestría
  5. sway
    Synonym: influjo
  6. ownership
    Synonyms: propiedad, juro

Derived terms

[edit]
  • autodominio
  • dominio público

Related terms

[edit]
  • dominar

[edit]
